envelope.text: past the call: nano-ros lends them

why:
phase-428 W5 (2026-09-06) — ledgering a recorded sweep finding. RANKED-9. Two of the seven discarding call sites are here — `packages/api/nros-cpp/include/rclcpp/rclcpp.hpp:849` (poll form) and `:861` (callback form) — each dropping the create's `Result` with `(void)` and returning a non-null pointer to an entity whose `initialized_` is false. SILENTLY WRONG; `[[nodiscard]]` cannot reach an explicit `(void)` inside our own header. See `cpp:Node::create_publisher` for upstream's contract, the full call-site list and the disposition.

phase-428 Q1 (2026-09-06) -- adopt -> adopt-bounded, and the discarded-Result finding above is CLOSED: every `create_*` in the adapter now goes through `detail::require_created` (`packages/api/nros-cpp/include/rclcpp/rclcpp.hpp:382`), which calls `abort_failed_create` (`:374`, `NROS_RCLCPP_ABORT_FAILED_CREATE`) instead of handing back a pointer to a dead entity. The line numbers in that paragraph are pre-fix.

WHAT IS ADOPTED: the name, the call shape (name first, `shared_ptr` back), the poll-style and callback-style overloads. THE ENVELOPE, and where the compiler points: the handler signature. Ours hands the request and response BY REFERENCE into caller-owned storage -- `void(const S::Request&, S::Response&)` -- because a per-request heap allocation on the delivery path is exactly what RFC-0022 forbids.

THE REFUSAL SITE: `packages/api/nros-cpp/include/rclcpp/rclcpp.hpp:953-957` -- a third `create_service` overload, enabled only for a callable that is neither a QoS nor convertible to our handler type, whose body is `static_assert(detail::refuse<F>::value, NROS_RCLCPP_REFUSE_SHARED_PTR_SERVICE_CALLBACK)` (`:955`; message `packages/api/nros-cpp/include/rclcpp/logging.hpp:245`). So upstream's `[](const std::shared_ptr<Req>, std::shared_ptr<Resp>) {...}` is not `no matching function` -- it is a diagnostic naming the constraint and the by-reference signature to change to. Probe: `packages/api/nros-cpp/tests/compile/ros2_refuse_service_callback_probe.cpp`. The name is adopt-bounded rather than refuse-loud because the refusal is on ONE overload of a working verb; a row's disposition is per key, and the key is the verb.

AMENDED 2026-09-21 (phase-456 W5): the two overloads now return DIFFERENT types, and that is the item's substance rather than a detail.

The CALLBACK form returns `Service<S>::SharedPtr`, which is `nros::ServiceHandle<S>` — two words over `{executor, handle_id}`, because the arena owns the server and (W3) the handler, so there is no C++ object to point at. The POLL form returns `nros::Owned<nros::PollService<S>>` — the poll server BY VALUE, with an `operator->` so the documented `service->take_request(...)` drain keeps working.

They could not stay one type. W3 recorded the collision: one alias cannot be both an arena handle and a pointer to a poll object, and while it was both, `take_request()` was offered on objects whose storage the arena never filled. The poll form has no upstream signature (upstream REQUIRES a handler), so its return type claims nothing against rclcpp; the callback form keeps the adopted shape with the handle substituted for the `shared_ptr`, which is the same substitution `cpp:Node::create_subscription` carries.

The refusal overload and its probe are unchanged.

phase-488 (2026-10-21), measured on the stock ros2/examples ports in `packages/api/nros-cpp/tests/compile/rclcpp-examples/` (edit counts in its `edits.json`). OVERRIDDEN, the phase-417 W2.c refusal of upstream's `shared_ptr` handler shape. Its two reasons were a per-request HEAP allocation and a SECOND delivery path. Neither holds for the shape as now taken (hosted, function pointer or capture-less lambda, with or without the leading `std::shared_ptr<rmw_request_id_t>`): the request and response stay the trampoline's own locals, each `shared_ptr` LENDS one through a no-op deleter, and the control block a `shared_ptr` must allocate comes from a buffer in the same frame (`rclcpp::detail::FrameBlock`). The arena calls the same trampoline signature and the bytes go through the same deserialize -> handler -> serialize sequence. The stock `minimal_service` went from 13 edited lines to 3 (the 3 are its global `Node::SharedPtr`, see `cpp:Node::make_shared`). THE BOUND, loud rather than silent: upstream lets a handler KEEP the pointer, and here the object dies with the frame, so a handler that retains one aborts the process with `NROS_RCLCPP_REFUSE_RETAINED_SERVICE_PTR` instead of leaving a dangling pointer (held by `service_shared_ptr_handler_runtime.cpp`); the request header was zero-filled then, because the dispatch path carried no writer GUID or sequence number to a server handler (issue 2081 since fills it -- see the paragraph below). Still refused, with `NROS_RCLCPP_REFUSE_SERVICE_CALLBACK_SHAPE`: a handler with STATE (capturing lambda, `std::bind`), because the arena stores one function pointer per service -- `ros2_refuse_service_callback_probe.cpp` now holds that shape.

phase-488 W3 (2026-10-25) -- that refusal is LIFTED. Porting Autoware's `autoware_external_cmd_selector` needed `create_service(name, std::bind(&X::f, this, _1, _2), rmw_qos_profile_services_default, group)` with a handler returning `bool`. A handler with state is now copied into the service's arena entry (`register_service_raw_capturing`, the capture region subscriptions and timers already have, destroyed exactly once with the entry) and dispatched through `detail::stateful_service_trampoline`, in all three shapes; its return value is discarded, as upstream's `std::function<void(...)>` discards it. `NROS_RCLCPP_REFUSE_SERVICE_CALLBACK_SHAPE` now refuses only a callable invocable as none of the shapes, which is what the probe holds. Runtime: `ament_port_surface_runtime.cpp`. The CLIENT half (`create_client<S>(name, callback)` with a shared-future callback) is untouched and still carries `NROS_RCLCPP_REFUSE_SHARED_PTR_SERVICE_CALLBACK`.

issue 2081 (2026-10-26) -- the three-argument form's `std::shared_ptr<rmw_request_id_t>` request header now carries the request's id: the requesting client's writer GUID and the sequence number that client assigned, as the RMW backend reported it (zenoh: the query attachment; Cyclone DDS: stock `rmw_cyclonedds_cpp`'s layout; XRCE-DDS: the Agent's `SampleIdentity`), for both the frame-lent function-pointer handler and the arena-captured stateful one. A backend that reports no id leaves it zero. `rmw_request_id_t` is one struct shared with the C API and the RMW ABI under one include guard. Held by `service_request_header_runtime.cpp` in `just check cpp`.
